headline: Chip shares led a rebound on Wednesday

sections.text: CoreWeave (a company that rents out AI computing power) jumped about 25% after beating its sales forecast and raising its outlook, and every company in the main US chip index rose; the S&P 500 gained 1.3% to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq 1.6% and the VIX 'fear gauge' fell 10% to 17.49. In London the FTSE 100 rose 0.8% to 10,835.47 and the FTSE 250 0.7%, with oil companies helped by Brent crude climbing 1.4% to $92.76 a barrel after Iran said its enriched nuclear material will not leave the country. The Stoxx 600 (up 0.7%) and Germany's DAX (up 1.2%) both closed at records. Rates are still the worry: futures put about a 90% chance on a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December, the dollar firmed, the pound slipped 0.5% to $1.3270 and gold fell 1.2%; the US bond market was shut for Veterans Day, so the 10-year yield stays at Tuesday's 4.98%.

UK growth figures for July to September come out at 07:00 today, with forecasters expecting about 0.7% growth on the quarter, and US producer prices follow on Friday. Greencoat UK Wind goes ex-dividend today (anyone buying from today misses the next payout, due 27 Nov). Next week brings UK jobs data and Nvidia's results (about 21:20 UK) on 17 Nov, then SSE and Severn Trent half-year results and UK inflation on 18 Nov. The Fed decides on 9 Dec, and the Bank of England and ECB both on 17 Dec, with markets now seeing roughly a two-in-three chance of another Bank of England rise.
Reading results: what a company's quarterly report tells you, with Vestas as the example. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

standfirst: The S&P 500 rose 1.3% and the FTSE 100 0.8% after strong results from CoreWeave revived hopes for AI spending, even though markets still expect a US rate rise in December.
